bib.title: GLM-130B: An Open Bilingual Pre-trained Model

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; Table 12 (74 MIP dataset names) and Table 15 (per-task MMLU) read but not itemised.

question: How can an open 100B-scale dense bilingual (English/Chinese) LLM at least as good as GPT-3 davinci be pre-trained stably and made cheap enough to run on affordable GPUs?
hypothesis: A bidirectional GLM backbone with blank-infilling plus a small share of multi-task instruction pre-training, stabilised by DeepNorm and embedding gradient shrink, can match or beat GPT-3 175B at 130B parameters.
contributions: Open-source a 130B bilingual dense model (weights, code, training logs, toolkit, lessons learned)
Training-stability recipe for 100B scale: DeepNorm Post-LN plus Embedding Layer Gradient Shrink (alpha=0.1) with FP16 mixed precision
Platform-aware 3D parallel configuration (4-way tensor, 8-way pipeline, PipeDream-Flush) that fixes the model shape (70 layers)
INT4 weight-only quantization without post-training, enabling inference on 4x RTX 3090 or 8x RTX 2080 Ti
Evaluation on 112 tasks plus bias and toxicity benchmarks; lessons learned (Appendix B.10)

method.summary: A 130B-parameter, 70-layer bidirectional GLM (autoregressive blank infilling with [MASK] and [gMASK]) trained for 400B tokens on a bilingual corpus with 5% multi-task instruction pre-training (MIP), on 96 DGX-A100 40G nodes in about 60 days. Stability came from DeepNorm Post-LN and embedding gradient shrink under FP16 mixed precision. The weights are then quantized to INT4 (absmax, weight-only) with activations kept in FP16.
method.task: next-token / blank-infilling pretraining of a bilingual LLM, plus INT4 post-hoc weight quantization

datasets.name: The Pile (train split), English
datasets.size: 1.2T (as printed; tokens or bytes not stated)

datasets.name: MIP: 74 prompted datasets (T0/PromptSource NLU and NLG, DeepStruct information extraction)
datasets.size: 5% of training tokens; per-dataset truncation printed as '10,0000' samples (T0 sets, presumably 100,000) and '20,0000' (IE sets, presumably 200,000), '50,0000' for KELM and PropBank (presumably 500,000)
datasets.split: approximately 36% of the samples in each dataset seen
datasets.source: Sanh et al. 2022; Bach et al. 2022; Wang et al. 2022a
datasets.preprocessing: Jinja templates; DeepStruct prompts hand-written by the authors. Mistake: both T0 train and zero-shot-transfer datasets were included and DeepStruct excluded until fixed at about 23k steps; the model kept training on the corrected data

datasets.name: Eval: LAMBADA, Pile test (18 sub-sets), MMLU (57 tasks), BIG-bench-lite (24 tasks), CLUE (7) and FewCLUE (5), CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet, ETHOS, RealToxicPrompts, GEM (WebNLG, E2E, WikiLingua), SuperGLUE, others
datasets.split: dev sets for CLUE/FewCLUE; test for Pile; 5000 random WikiLingua test examples
datasets.preprocessing: 13-gram overlap check for LAMBADA and CLUE (minimal overlap); Pile, MMLU, BIG-bench held out or released after corpus crawl

models.name: GLM-130B
models.architecture: bidirectional GLM (blank infilling), Post-LN with DeepNorm, RoPE, GeGLU FFN
models.tokenizer: icetk-based SentencePiece unigram, trained on 25GB bilingual corpus; adds [MASK], [gMASK], <sop>, <eop>, <eos>
models.vocab: 150000 in icetk, first 20000 are image tokens, remaining 130000 text tokens used
models.layers: 70 (9x8-2, one layer removed from each pipeline end)

other.DeepNorm init: Xavier normal with scale (2N)^(-1/2) on ffn, v_proj, out_proj; biases zero

other.note: authors could not run it themselves; numbers taken from OPT paper and others

other.use: PE and FFN ablation, pre-trained on a random 50G Chinese-English corpus

models.name: GLM-10B (English-only)
models.init_from: released GLM-10B without MIP; MIP variant initialised from a middle-stage checkpoint

other.use: ablation of GLM objective versus MIP

training.objective: Autoregressive blank infilling (95% of tokens): [MASK] on 30% of sequences (Poisson lambda=3 spans totalling 15% of input), [gMASK] on 70% (uniform-length long blank at end, prefix kept); plus 5% multi-task instruction pre-training
training.lr_schedule: warm up from 1e-7 to 8e-5 over first 0.5% samples, then 10x cosine decay (lr_decay_samples 197753905)
training.warmup: LR warmup over 0.5% of samples (lr_warmup_samples 1098632); batch size warmup from 192 to 4224 over first 2.5% samples (rampup_batch_size 192, 24, 5493164)
training.seq_len: 2048 ([gMASK] uses 2048 context; [MASK] and MIP use 512 and concatenate four samples to 2048)
training.precision: FP16 mixed precision (Apex O2): FP16 forward/backward, FP32 optimizer states and master weights; attention softmax in FP32
training.regularisation: gradient clipping 1.0; Embedding Layer Gradient Shrink alpha=0.1; DeepNorm
training.hardware: 96 NVIDIA DGX-A100 nodes (8x40G), world size 768; TP=4, PP=8, DP=24, ZeRO stage 1, PipeDream-Flush from DeepSpeed
training.compute: 442.4 MWh electricity over the 60-day course; 257.01 metric tons CO2 (0.5810 kg/kWh)

inference.decoding: Zero/few-shot scoring: option log-likelihood for multiple choice (BIG-bench, MMLU next-token A/B/C/D probability); greedy decoding for BIG-bench generation; nucleus sampling for RealToxicPrompts
inference.samples: 25 continuations for each of 10K random prompts (RealToxicPrompts); median over 5 or 15 prompts for NLI; 1-shot demos randomly sampled from train for GEM
inference.prompting: Zero-shot to 5-shot; PromptSource prompts; English prompts and verbalizers used for Chinese CLUE; MMLU 1-shot example in Appendix C.6; PaLM-style prompts 'Summarize the following article:' and 'Verbalize:' for GEM

parameters.INT4 quantization: weight-only absmax, per-row, linear layers only; embeddings, LayerNorm and biases left in FP16; two INT4 packed per INT8; dequantized to FP16 at runtime
parameters.Pile eval: [gMASK], 1024 context tokens bidirectional then 1024 tokens scored autoregressively

other.inference engine: FasterTransformer C++ reimplementation (two months of work)

metrics.name: Pile BPB
metrics.definition: bits-per-byte, weighted average over 18 shared sub-sets by ratio in the Pile train set

metrics.name: CLUE/FewCLUE
metrics.definition: accuracy, EM for DRCD and CMRC2018, zero-shot on dev sets

eval.protocol: Single run, no seeds or significance tests. GPT-3 numbers mostly from literature or OpenAI API; OPT/BLOOM from OPT paper, BigScience sheets or own HF runs. English zero-shot restricted to datasets with domain transfer from MIP; fixed-label tasks such as NLI excluded from the main results.

availability.weights: public on application under a license forbidding harmful use

limits: Few-shot gains are smaller than GPT-3's; the authors conjecture the cause (bidirectionality, zero-shot-only MIP) without testing it
MIP covers 74 datasets, so zero-shot comparisons are restricted by the authors' own criterion; SuperGLUE and NLI results are explicitly not zero-shot
Only 400B tokens were seen (about 200B English); authors concede under-training and weak closed-book QA (Natural Questions)
Only part of CLUE/FewCLUE and 24 of 150 BIG-bench tasks were evaluated
OPT-175B could not be run by the authors; its numbers come from other sources, GPT-3 mostly from literature
No seeds or confidence intervals; ablations of the GLM objective and MIP were done at 10B, not 130B
Pile BPB is on 18 of 22 sub-sets, compared to numbers copied from Jurassic-1/GPT-3
Bias results use English-centric benchmarks; Chinese biases are not tested
BLOOM-176B comparison uses BF16 and HF implementation; speedup figures partly reflect implementation, not architecture
Several explanations (why GLM quantizes to INT4, outlier meaning) are speculative

problems: Text extraction scrambles tables and figure data (Fig 8 CLUE bars, Table 2 layout) so values were read by position; Table 2 row layout was reconstructed.
Paper says 'Figure 17' for chain-of-thought results in C.14 but they are Figure 18 (author typo).
Section 4 text says 4 x RTX 3090 Ti in some places and 3090 (24G) in others; the abstract says RTX 3090.

Appendix C.1 says 'by a mistake' the MIP included T0 zero-shot-transfer sets; fixed at around 23k steps, but Fig 21 timeline says a mistake was found after about 20,000 steps and corrected data did not make it 'forget'.
Table 11 contains duplicated lines (tokenizer_type, weight_decay) from layout; no embedded instructions found.
